payload.title: Record where hyp keeps the record off every code branch
payload.body: Part of #181, order 1 of #180. A design record: its one question was settled by argument in the grill of 2026-11-14, with the session as evidence, so it has no lines; its cases go to the lines of the build Goal that follows it in this store. A settled shape, not a question: the ref is hidden (refs/hyp/record), not a branch, so no GitHub button deletes, merges or checks it out, and a plain git fetch does not bring it; hyp sync does.

why: Grilled in session 2026-11-14 on #181; the owner approved the title and body.

payload.title: hyp keeps the record apart from every code branch, owned by one module: the log, the files it names and the commits it cites
payload.body:
Part of #180 (order 1); builds #181. Covers #179, #152, #177's landing step and part of #151; it decides the record for #168, whose filters (status --all, cites across stores, alias scope) are a later Goal. The candidate is a hyp commit; go test on its base and on the candidate is the instrument.

The record: every event of every store of one git repository, the bytes of every file an event names (evidence, an Experiment's records, a subject's patch and files, also of retracted Results), each bundle an event pins, and every commit a Hypothesis subject names, kept by hyp as commits on the hidden ref refs/hyp/record, which no branch holds. A record repository is a git repository that holds that ref.

Decided in the grill of 2026-11-14 (design record record-design in this store, h-ref selected): a write is durable once it exits 0; one record per repository, and a store keeps its name, its folder's path from the repository root; hyp sync [REMOTE] fetches the remote's record, joins the two logs as a set by id and pushes, and the hyp-goal-run skill runs it at every stop; the record keeps only cited files, and git ignores every other file under .tree/evidence/ (#152); an evidence pointer stores its file's sha256; a sandbox clone, a git repository with no record ref and a directory with no git use the work-tree .tree/ as today; hyp import [REF:]PATH... names its stores and may run again. After this Goal merges, the owner imports this repository's five stores and tag g-akjjf8/record; old .tree/ folders stay as frozen copies, cited files tracked. Accepted: a hyp built before this change reads only those copies, sees no later event, and rejects an event that stores an evidence sha256. Reopens ADR 0022 and 0023 (unmerged); a new ADR records it; the glossary gains Record and Record repository.

Each Experiment's rubric also runs hyp import in a sandbox clone of this repository and compares each Goal's node statuses with its work-tree store's.

Line 3 and the last sentence of line 9 hold on the base.

May change: hyp in this repository (cmd/, internal/, docs/), as commits on one local branch pushed as a PR the run never merges
May change: any text in skills/, README.md or AGENTS.md the change makes wrong
May change: this Goal's store, investigations/record, written with the installed hyp on a branch cut from main that holds only .tree/ changes, in its own worktree, pushed as a record PR the owner merges at every stop
Read only: the events and evidence of every other store under investigations/; every frozen recipe version under recipes/ and investigations/*/recipes/; the tags g-akjjf8/record, g-akjjf8/candidates and goal-prompt/subject-*
Never: run a candidate's hyp so that it writes a ref, a record or a store in this clone or on origin; its tests and Experiments use fixtures, temporary repositories and sandbox clones
Never: replace the installed hyp binary at ~/.local/bin/hyp
Never: edit or remove a line of any events file
Never: merge a PR

lines.text: [P] In a record repository, an event a write exited 0 on, and the bytes of each file it names, are printed by `hyp show` and `hyp status` run in its store's folder in every worktree of that clone, also after a branch is deleted, squash- or rebase-merged, reset or checked out, after `git clean -fdx` and `git gc --prune=now`, and after the worktree the write ran in is removed. A later change or removal of a work-tree file the event names changes nothing those commands print for it.

[P] In a record repository, every commit a Hypothesis subject names stays reachable from a ref, and `hyp sandbox create --base` with it succeeds, also after every branch that held it is deleted, squash- or rebase-merged, and after `git gc --prune=now`.

[N] No command reads part of a write: a write stopped after any of its steps and before it exits leaves the record holding either the whole event, with the bytes of every file it names, or nothing of it.

[P] Two writes run at once from two worktrees of one record repository both apply, and each new id sorts after every id its store held before that write; the refusal when no ULID sorts after the newest id stays.

[P] After `hyp sync REMOTE`, the local record and REMOTE's record each hold the union of both, every event, named file and subject commit, also when each side holds events the other lacks, and both replay to the same projection. A fresh `git clone` of REMOTE followed by `hyp sync origin` prints what the syncing clone prints. On a REMOTE with no record, `hyp sync` pushes the local one; a REMOTE that refuses the ref gives exit 3.

[N] The record holds no file but those an event names and the files of each bundle an event pins. `hyp init`, and `hyp import` for each store it imports, write an ignore rule under which git ignores every file under that store's `.tree/evidence/`, and `hyp import` untracks each file there that no event names, leaving it on disk.

[P] A Result's `questionable` and `uncontained` flags, and the warnings `hyp check` prints for it, are the same from every checkout of a record repository, whatever its `recipes/`, `rubrics/` and `.tree/evidence/` hold: the record keeps each bundle an event pins.

[P] `hyp import [REF:]PATH...` adds to the record every event of each named work-tree store, read from the checkout or from REF, that the record lacks, with the bytes of each file those events name and their subject commits; running it again adds nothing, and each imported Goal's node statuses equal those its work-tree store replays to.

[N] In a record repository, a write in a folder where store discovery finds a work-tree `.tree/` holding an event the record lacks is refused with exit 1, naming `hyp import`; `hyp check` reports that store, and each checked-out bundle whose hash differs from a pin of the same ref. `hyp init` in a git repository makes it a record repository. In a git repository with no record ref, and where no `.git` is at or above the current directory, hyp reads and writes the work-tree `.tree/` as on the base.
[N] No non-test Go file outside package `record` contains the string `.tree` or `.git`, and none outside packages `record` and `sandbox` runs git; a go test over the source fails on any other.

payload.title: hyp keeps the record apart from every code branch: one history of every store, by name and id
payload.body:
Part of #180 (order 2); builds #181. It replaces build Goal G-SZCBXZ in this store, whose lines 1, 5, 8 and 9 left their range open, so each review in runs 4 and 5 found a new case. G-SZCBXZ stays in_progress, and no run acts on it.

The record is that of G-SZCBXZ's body and design record G-4N85GM (h-ref selected): every event of every store of one git repository, the bytes of every file an event names, each bundle an event pins, and every commit a subject names, kept as commits on the hidden ref refs/hyp/record. A record repository is a git repository that holds that ref. The record is the one history of #168: every event once, by an id unique across the repository. Its filters, the owner's overview and the relations between Goals, are a later Goal.

The owner decided in this grill on 2026-11-14: a store's name is its folder's resolved path, and a store folder's name is plain; every file path keeps any path git can hold; hyp import adds each event once, by id, with its bytes or not at all; a read during hyp's own snapshot prune is covered.

The base is commit c5b34da6e8eea5b507bed00d624b46afddbe4a44 (h-record-16 of G-SZCBXZ) on feat/record. Its tests that a later import adds what an earlier import lacked go with the first candidate. Lines 5 and 7 hold on the base. Line 1 covers that an event's files survive in one clone, not how two contents at one path show after a sync. A store folder moved or renamed after its events are in the record is not a case. Line 8 does not cover other bytes at the path of a file an event names, and a store with a named file, bundle or subject commit missing from every source is not a case. The run continues on feat/record and PR #187, merges main into it, from 7237c49 with #174's hold rule on, and never rebases it, and gives each Hypothesis an alias that starts with h-rec2-.

Each Experiment's rubric also runs hyp import in a temporary clone of this repository and compares each Goal's node statuses with its work-tree store's.

May change: hyp in this repository (cmd/, internal/, docs/), as commits on the local branch feat/record pushed to PR #187, which the run never merges
May change: any text in skills/, README.md or AGENTS.md the change makes wrong
May change: this Goal's store, investigations/record, written with the installed hyp on a branch cut from main that holds only .tree/ changes, in its own worktree, pushed as a record PR the owner merges at every stop
Read only: the events and evidence of every other store under investigations/; every frozen recipe version under recipes/ and investigations/*/recipes/; the tags g-akjjf8/record, g-akjjf8/candidates and goal-prompt/subject-*
Never: run a candidate's hyp so that it writes a ref, a record or a store in this clone or on origin; its tests and Experiments use fixtures, temporary repositories and sandbox clones
Never: replace the installed hyp binary at ~/.local/bin/hyp
Never: edit or remove a line of any events file
Never: merge a PR

lines.text: [P] In a record repository, an event a write exited 0 on is printed by `hyp show` and `hyp status` run in its store's folder in every worktree of that clone, and the bytes of each file it names, at whatever path git can hold, by `hyp show`, also after a branch is deleted, squash- or rebase-merged, reset or checked out, after `git clean -fdx` and `git gc --prune=now`, and after the worktree the write ran in is removed. A later change or removal of a work-tree file it names changes nothing they print.

[P] In a record repository, every commit that the base of a Hypothesis subject or of a Result's run subject names stays reachable from a ref, and `hyp sandbox create --base` with it succeeds, also after every branch that held it is deleted, squash- or rebase-merged, and after `git gc --prune=now`.

[N] No command reads part of a write, an import or a sync: one stopped after any of its steps and before it exits leaves the record holding either each whole event it adds, with the bytes of every file that event names, or nothing of it, and a read run while another command writes, or prunes hyp's snapshots, prints the record as it was before or after that write.

[P] Two writes run at once from two worktrees of one record repository both apply, and each new id sorts after every id the record held before that write, whichever store holds that id; the refusal when no ULID sorts after the newest id stays. Only a write makes a new id: hyp import and hyp sync add events with their own ids. It covers when writes happen, not what a write names.

[P] After `hyp sync REMOTE`, the local record and REMOTE's record each hold the union of both, every event, named file and subject commit, also when each side holds events the other lacks, and both replay to the same projection. A fresh `git clone` of REMOTE followed by `hyp sync origin` prints what the syncing clone prints. On a REMOTE with no record, `hyp sync` pushes the local one; a REMOTE that refuses the ref gives exit 3. It does not ask how two contents at one path show after a sync.

[N] The record holds no file but its events, those an event names, the files of each bundle an event pins and the copies sync keeps; `hyp init` and `hyp import` make git ignore every file under each store's `.tree/evidence/`, and `hyp import` untracks each one no event names. `hyp init` and `hyp import` exit 1 and write nothing for a store folder below the repository root whose path has a character other than ASCII letters, digits, ., _, -, @ and /, a .git, . or .. part, or a part that differs only in case from another in its folder.

[P] A Result's `questionable` and `uncontained` flags, and the warnings `hyp check` prints about it, are the same from every checkout of a record repository, whatever its `recipes/`, `rubrics/` and `.tree/evidence/` hold: the record keeps each bundle an event pins. It covers warnings about the Result, not a warning about a checked-out bundle that names the Result as its pinner.

[P] `hyp import [REF:]PATH...` adds to the record each event of each named work-tree store, from the checkout or from REF, whose id the record lacks, with the bytes of each file and bundle it names and its subject commits, and changes no event the record holds; when the record then holds no event of a store that the source lacks, its Goals' node statuses equal its work-tree store's. It exits 1 and adds nothing when a named file, bundle or subject commit is missing from the source or differs from a sha256 the event stores, or a named store holds an id another store holds.

[N] In a record repository, a write in a store whose work-tree `.tree/` holds an event the record lacks exits 1 naming `hyp import`, and `hyp check` reports that store and each checked-out bundle whose hash differs from its pin. A store's name is its folder's path from the root, links resolved, each name spelled as its directory lists it; each command run in or naming a store folder outside the repository exits 1. `hyp init`, `hyp import` or `hyp sync` makes a git repository a record repository; a sandbox clone, a repository with no record ref, or no `.git` keeps the work-tree `.tree/`.

[N] No non-test Go file outside package `record` holds a string literal that contains `.tree` or `.git`, and none outside packages `record` and `sandbox` calls `exec.Command` or `exec.CommandContext` with the string literal "git" as its first argument; a go test over the source fails on any other. A string or command name built from parts, or a command run through a shell or a full path, is not a case.

why: The owner's second grill of #181 on 2026-11-14: the record as a build Goal with bounded lines.
